scope: Both revised originals inspected directly at original detail against the preceding rejected originals and canonical Christ identity previously inspected.

candidates.alt: Jesus watches a servant pour water from a clay pitcher into one of six large stone jars.
candidates.caption: Jesus instructs the servants at Cana to fill the six stone waterpots. Their appearances and the courtyard arrangement are artistic interpretations of John 2.
candidates.findings: Exactly six large stone openings now visible: back-left, left-middle, front-left, back-center, receiving jar right and front-center. The separate pouring clay pitcher is correctly not counted. Christ identity and expression preserved; servant is sufficiently distinct. Hands, stream and receiving jar are physically coherent, with photographic skin, water and materials. Previous extra-jar defect resolved.

candidates.alt: Jesus addresses departing disciples on a rural road as an older man looks back toward Him.
candidates.caption: Jesus sends the Twelve to proclaim the kingdom and heal. This illustration shows part of the departing group; their appearances, gestures and the road are artistic interpretations.
candidates.findings: Nearest disciple now reads as a distinctly older balding man with gray beard, different cheek/brow and nose structure; previous Christ-duplicate defect resolved. Left foreground disciple has broadly similar regional hair/beard styling but sufficiently different profile and shorter beard; no remaining material identity duplication observed. Christ's recognizable face remains unchanged. Reciprocal gaze, departing bodies and visible hands remain coherent with photographic texture.

overall: Both corrected originals pass technical review. No owner approval inferred.
